title: Optomechanical systems with a Fano membrane in the middle
authors: Lei Du, Aymeric Frerejean, Witlef Wieczorek, Janine Splettstoesser, Juliette Monsel
abstract: Conventional membrane-in-the-middle (MIM) optomechanical systems offer limited control over the optical linewidth, which can limit their performance when operating in the unresolved-sideband regime. We investigate cavity optomechanics with a photonic-crystal Fano membrane placed at the center of a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity. In contrast to a conventional dielectric membrane, the photonic-crystal membrane supports a localized optical resonance, which hybridizes with the cavity field and enables spectral engineering of the relevant optical modes. Besides the usual dispersive optomechanical coupling associated with cavity-length changes, the membrane motion also modifies the Fano-mode resonance and its hybridization with the cavity field. We consider two limits set by the membrane reflectivity: a transparent-membrane regime with a single FP-like mode, and a reflective-membrane regime with two coupled subcavity modes. In the latter case, only the symmetric cavity mode hybridizes with the Fano mode, while the antisymmetric mode remains decoupled. Using quantum Langevin equations together with a transfer-matrix description of the optical scattering problem, we show that the Fano-induced hybridization can generate narrow optical normal modes that remain efficiently accessible to the external drive for experimentally realistic parameters. These modes can provide effective sideband resolution and enable ground-state cooling of the membrane motion even when the bare cavity is in the unresolved-sideband regime. Our results establish Fano MIM systems as a promising platform for spectral and optomechanical engineering.
summary: This paper investigates using a photonic-crystal Fano membrane within an optomechanical cavity to overcome limitations in linewidth control. By modeling both transparent and reflective membrane regimes, the authors show that the unique hybridization provided by the Fano resonance generates narrow optical modes. These engineered modes enable efficient ground-state cooling of the mechanical oscillator even when standard cavity parameters suggest otherwise.
main_problem: Conventional optomechanical systems suffer from limited control over optical linewidth, which restricts their performance when attempting ground-state cooling in the unresolved-sideband regime.
main_result: The incorporation of a photonic-crystal Fano membrane enables spectral engineering, generating narrow optical normal modes that maintain efficient coupling to external drives and allow for ground-state cooling even when the bare cavity is in the unresolved sideband regime.
method: The authors employ quantum Langevin equations combined with a transfer-matrix description of the optical scattering problem to analyze the system dynamics across different reflectivity regimes.
model_or_system: The system is an optomechanical setup involving a Fabry-Pérot cavity containing a photonic-crystal Fano membrane. The model considers two limits: a transparent-membrane regime (single mode) and a reflective-membrane regime (two coupled subcavity modes).
key_observables: Final phonon occupation number ($ ar{n}_{fin}$), effective sideband resolution ($\kappa^-$), and the required laser power for cooling.
important_parameters: Membrane reflectivity, coupling strengths ($g_{d,0}, g_{\lambda,0}$), cavity loss rates ($\kappa$), and mechanical frequency ($\Omega_m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linearizing the dynamics in the weak-coupling regime and assumes that the Fano membrane provides a frequency-dependent optical response superior to conventional dielectric membranes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates schematics of the setup, detailing diagrams for both the transparent-membrane (TM) limit (single mode coupling) and the reflective-membrane (RM) limit ($\hat{a}_L$, $\hat{a}_R$ subcavities).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitations of conventional MIM systems. It then develops the theoretical framework by analyzing the Hamiltonian and dynamics for both TM and RM regimes using Langevin equations. Finally, it derives key results showing how Fano-induced hybridization enables superior cooling performance.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced topics in cavity quantum electrodynamics (cavity QED) and open quantum systems, specifically focusing on engineered coupling mechanisms to enhance ground-state cooling capabilities beyond standard limits.
